note: gText is a locale STRING-TRANSLATION utility (built on core locale), NOT a fonts/typography module. It adds a 'Translating texts' UI at /admin/config/texts (configure route gtext.translate), a Twig gtext() helper / 'gtext' service, and optional Google Translate machine translation. Its only config is gtext.settings:google_api_key (string), with NO config/install (absent by default): with a key it uses the official google/cloud-translate client, without a key it uses a free translate.google.com fallback (<=1000 chars). Permissions: 'access gtext translate strings' and 'access gtext translate'. The Google key settings form is at /admin/config/gtext/settings. Medium cases seed a known google_api_key and read it back; hard cases set the key to a target value or clear it, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal gtext (gText) module do, and where is its main configuration/translation page?
evals.expected_output: gText is a locale string-translation utility built on core locale. Its main UI is 'Translating texts' at /admin/config/texts (configure route gtext.translate), where you browse translatable source strings (grouped by context) and translate them per language. It also adds a Twig gtext() helper and optional Google Translate machine translation. It is about text/string translation, not fonts.

evals.prompt: In gtext, which config object and key hold the Google Translate API key, and what happens if no key is configured?
evals.expected_output: The key is gtext.settings:google_api_key (a string; there is no config/install so the object is absent until set). With a key, gText uses the official google/cloud-translate client. With no key it falls back to a free unofficial translate.google.com endpoint limited to 1000 characters per request.

evals.prompt: Which permissions does the gtext module define, and what does each control?
evals.expected_output: gText defines 'access gtext translate strings' (access to the /admin/config/texts string-translation UI, marked restricted) and 'access gtext translate' (adds the inline 'translate' buttons to config-translation and entity-translation forms). The Google key settings page itself is gated by core 'administer site configuration'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, gtext has a Google Translate API key configured. Inspect the live configuration and report the exact key value.
This site's gtext is configured to use the official Google Cloud Translate client rather than the free fallback. Inspect the running configuration and report the configured Google API key.
evals.expected_output: gtext.settings:google_api_key is set to AIzaSyGTEXT-provider-key-456, so gText uses the official google/cloud-translate client (a non-empty key switches off the free fallback).

evals.prompt: Configure the gtext module on this Drupal site to use the Google Translate API key AIzaSyGTEXT-task-target-key-789 . Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set gtext.settings:google_api_key to exactly AIzaSyGTEXT-task-target-key-789 and save (e.g. \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('gtext.settings')->set('google_api_key', 'AIzaSyGTEXT-task-target-key-789')->save()).

evals.prompt: gtext on this site currently has a Google Translate API key set. Turn off the paid Google client so the module uses its free translation fallback instead, by clearing the configured key. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Clear gtext.settings:google_api_key (set it to an empty string, or delete the config object) so the value is empty/absent; gText then uses the free translate.google.com fallback.
